title: Add name-based login, streak points, and weekly user ranking (rank module)

requirements.text: Add an initial Login screen that is shown on app start when no user name has been set yet, with a single name input and a continue/login action. The login form must validate that the entered value is a “good name” (letters and spaces only, trimmed, non-empty, and within a reasonable length) and display an English validation error when invalid. After a successful login, persist the user name in app state so it remains available throughout the app and across refreshes via the existing IndexedDB persistence.

quotes: now at the starting make a login page and save the name of the user throught the end login page should consist only your good name like example "chittya "

acceptanceCriteria: When the app loads with no saved user name, the Login screen is displayed instead of the main app screens.
The Login screen contains only the user name field and a continue/login button (no extra required fields).
Name validation rejects empty input, whitespace-only input, and any characters outside A–Z/a–z and spaces, showing an English error message.
After successful login, the user name is stored in the persisted app state and remains after page refresh.
After login, the user can access the existing Home/Timetable/Settings flow as before.

requirements.text: Extend the frontend domain state and reducer to support a user profile and gamification fields needed for streak points, including at minimum: user name, total points, streak tracking metadata needed to compute a continuous day streak, and a record of which streak milestones have already been awarded so points are not repeatedly re-awarded for the same milestone.

quotes: if the user maintain countnous streak of 3 days give 5 points giveing a msg congo on your hatric if 6 days give 10 points

acceptanceCriteria: App state includes persisted fields for user name and points.
State updates for points and streak milestone awards are implemented via the existing reducer/action pattern (no ad-hoc mutation).
Existing persistence, load, and save flows continue to work without crashes after adding the new fields.

requirements.text: Implement continuous day streak detection based on recorded ClassEvent activity: treat a day as “completed” if at least one ClassEvent exists for that calendar date; compute the current streak as the number of consecutive completed days ending at today (using local time date strings already stored in events). When the streak reaches 3 days for the first time, award +5 points and show an English congratulatory message: “Congrats on your hat-trick! +5 points.” When the streak reaches 6 days for the first time, award +10 points and show an English congratulatory message: “Congrats on your 6-day streak! +10 points.”

quotes: if the user maintain countnous streak of 3 days give 5 points giveing a msg congo on your hatric if 6 days give 10 points

acceptanceCriteria: If the user has at least one class event on three consecutive dates ending today, the app awards exactly +5 points once and shows the hat-trick message once.
If the user has at least one class event on six consecutive dates ending today, the app awards exactly +10 points once and shows the 6-day streak message once.
Points are not re-awarded on subsequent app loads or subsequent events if the milestone was already awarded for the current/ongoing streak.
If a day is missed (no events on that date), the continuous day streak resets appropriately.
Milestone award logic is triggered in a deterministic place in the app flow (e.g., after saving Mark Today events) so that awarding occurs reliably.

requirements.text: Create a separate frontend folder named "rank" to contain all ranking-related UI and logic. Add a Rank screen that can be navigated to from the app (e.g., via a Settings link/button) without breaking existing navigation. The Rank screen must show an English weekly leaderboard list of users ordered by points for the current week, including each user’s rank number, display name, and points.

quotes: rank all the users once a week make separe folder "rank"

acceptanceCriteria: A new folder exists at frontend/src/rank (or equivalent under frontend/src) containing the rank page/components/modules.
The app provides a visible navigation entry point to the Rank screen (with English label, e.g., “Weekly Ranking”) and allows returning back.
The Rank screen renders a leaderboard ordered by points descending with clear rank numbering.
If no ranking data is available, the Rank screen shows an English empty state message.

requirements.text: Implement backend support for multi-user weekly ranking in the single Motoko actor (backend/main.mo): store users keyed by a stable identifier (principal when available, otherwise reject unauthenticated writes), store weekly points totals, and expose query/update methods to (a) register/update a user’s display name, (b) record earned points increments for the current week, and (c) fetch the current week’s ordered ranking list. The backend must compute the “current week” deterministically (e.g., by week-start timestamp) and ensure the ranking list reflects the current week only.

quotes: rank all the users once a week

acceptanceCriteria: backend/main.mo contains all backend logic (single-actor architecture preserved).
Backend provides a method to set/update the user’s display name tied to their identity.
Backend provides a method to add points for the current week for the caller.
Backend provides a query method that returns the current week ranking ordered by weekly points descending (and includes user display name + points).
Ranking is scoped to the current week only (previous weeks do not inflate current week totals).

requirements.text: Wire the frontend streak points awarding to the backend ranking system: when the app awards +5 or +10 points for a milestone, it must also submit the points increment to the backend for the logged-in user and ensure the user’s display name is registered/updated in the backend. The Rank screen must fetch the weekly ranking list from the backend and display it.

quotes: if the user maintain countnous streak of 3 days give 5 points... if 6 days give 10 points and rank all the users once a week

acceptanceCriteria: When a milestone award occurs, the frontend increments local points and also calls the backend to increment weekly points.
If backend calls fail, the app shows an English non-blocking error and does not crash; local points still remain consistent locally.
The Rank screen retrieves its leaderboard data from the backend and renders it.
User display name used in ranking matches the name saved from the Login screen.

requirements.text: Update local persistence and backup/restore to include the new user profile and gamification fields (user name, points, streak metadata, and milestone award state) while remaining backward compatible with existing stored data and older backups by merging missing fields with defaults.

quotes: save the name of the user throught the end

acceptanceCriteria: After updating, existing users with prior IndexedDB data can still load the app without errors and new fields are defaulted safely.
Exported backup files include the new user/profile and points fields.
Importing a backup correctly restores the user name and points fields.
Validation/migration logic tolerates backups created before this feature (missing new fields).

constraints: Do not edit any files under frontend/src/components/ui (shadcn components are read-only).
Do not edit immutable frontend paths listed by the platform (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts(x), frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx).
Keep all Motoko backend logic in the single actor file backend/main.mo (no additional backend services).
Use English for all user-facing text added by this change.
nonGoals: Do not add third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is allowed by the platform, but this feature is name-based).
Do not add push notifications or background scheduled jobs; weekly ranking must be computed deterministically when requested rather than relying on cron-like scheduling.
Do not change existing attendance calculation logic beyond what is necessary to detect day-based streaks from recorded events.
